title: Keyturn Vehicle Listing: Opening a Fault Record on a Vehicle's Condition History
content:
Where a fault has been found on a vehicle offered as a Keyturn Vehicle Listing, the marketplace holds it by opening a fault record on that vehicle's condition history. One record registers a single dated fault: the fault that was found, the host whose listing it belongs to, the earlier condition record the fault was carried across from, how the report was produced, and the photographs filed with it. The listing's own standing does not move, and what the host and the desk see afterwards is a new fault entry dated today on the vehicle's condition record, which every later reading of that vehicle's fault history includes.

A fault carried across from a condition record already standing on the vehicle is recorded under the fault that record names and through the channel that record was produced under, since the marketplace records a fault as the record that found it reports it.

### Making the entry

The desk unlocks the agent-side tool `log_vehicle_fault_a3e017f7` and calls it. One call opens one fault record.

### Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Form |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `vehicle_id` | The listing reference number of the vehicle the fault belongs to | Read from the vehicle listing lookup before the call |
| `customer_id` | The member reference number of the host who owns that listing | Read from the member profile lookup before the call |
| `source_inspection_id` | The reference number of the earlier condition record the fault is carried across from | Read from the vehicle condition record lookup before the call |
| `defect_code` | The fault this record registers | Exactly one of the values listed below |
| `inspection_channel` | Who produced the report | Exactly one of the values listed below |
| `attached_photo_count` | How many photographs are filed with this fault record | A whole number of photographs, with no decimal part, no unit suffix and no thousands separator; zero means no photograph is filed |

`defect_code` takes exactly one of: `none`, nothing was found and the record registers no fault at all; `tyre_tread`, a tyre is worn to or past its tread limit; `brake_wear`, brake pads, discs or fluid are worn past their service limit; `windscreen_chip`, the glass is chipped, starred or cracked; `warning_light`, a dashboard warning lamp is lit on the vehicle; `body_damage`, the bodywork, bumpers or panels are damaged; `missing_equipment`, equipment the class requires is absent from the vehicle; `open_recall`, the manufacturer has an unperformed safety recall on the vehicle.

`inspection_channel` takes exactly one of: `self_photo`, the host photographed the vehicle themselves; `partner_shop`, a partner workshop found it while the vehicle was with them; `mobile_inspector`, a marketplace inspector attending the vehicle found it; `telematics_report`, the fitted telematics unit reported it.

### What comes back

A confirmation sentence naming the reference number minted for the new fault record, the listing it was opened against, the fault registered and the number of photographs filed with it. The presence of that reference number in the sentence is what indicates the fault record now stands on the vehicle's condition history.
